title: SLO-as-Currency: per-endpoint spendable error budget and auctioned circuit-breaker policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current error-budgeting is passive — teams are informed when budgets burn but have limited programmatic levers to prioritize live traffic when capacity is constrained. During regional incidents we mix manual operator interventions with coarse failover rules that cause oscillation and poor tail latency for premium routes.

Goal: Define and prototype a per-endpoint 'SLO wallet' model where error budget is treated as a spendable currency that can be programmatically consumed to retain capacity. Introduce an auction-inspired circuit-breaker that lets endpoints bid for protection (graceful shedding, KV-cache reservation, preferential routing) in constrained states, with clear accounting, limits, and automated reconciliation. This should enable predictable, auditable prioritization during multiregion pressure while preserving overall platform safety.

Scope:
- SLI mapping and conversion to discrete "SLO units" per endpoint/model (monthly and rolling-30d budgets).
- Wallet accounting service and API (read-only for most teams, write via platform governance).
- Auctioned circuit-breaker mechanism: when a pool is overloaded, endpoints submit bids (SLO units) to request mitigation actions: pinned KV cache, reduced batching, reserved concurrency, failover to cold variants.
- Fail-safe caps, repayment logic, and operator override controls.
- Integration with Console dashboards and the billing-style ledger for audits.

Out of scope for initial spike: full enterprise billing integration, tenant-visible monetary charges, and on-prem packaging (we'll mock ledger data for private deployments).
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical conversion for latency and availability SLIs -> SLO units with worked examples for chat and embeddings routes
Implement a lightweight wallet prototype that can read/write SLO unit balances for endpoint records in staging
Create auction flow simulator that runs against historical traffic to show expected allocations and edge cases (oscillation, starvation)
Instrument console view showing per-endpoint wallet balance, recent bids, and outcome of auctions
Establish safety caps: no single endpoint can spend more than X% of pool budget; operator override path documented
Run a chaos test in a controlled region failure and show end-to-end behavior matches policy (logs, reconciliation, metrics)
design_notes: SLO units are an abstract integer currency; conversion uses both burn-rate and request-fidelity multipliers. Example: a chat route with tail-latency SLO 99th=250ms translates to 1 unit per 1k requests at baseline; heavy multimodal requests multiply unit cost.
Wallet service will be a thin eventual-consistent store with optimistic concurrency; authoritative ledger entries recorded to our auditing pipeline for forensic queries.

Auction mechanism: sealed-bid second-price style to discourage overbidding. Bids are per-minute timeboxes and tied to a candidate mitigation action (e.g., reserve-kv, pin-variant, reserve-concurrency).
Mitigation action catalog must be limited and idempotent — start with a small action set (reserve-kv, reserve-concurrency, model-variant-pin, route-reprioritize).
Fail-safes: hard caps on total spend per endpoint and per-customer; automated repayment is done by deficit credits accrued when SLO unit replenishment occurs (rolling window).

Regional behavior: auctions run per-pool (region or AZ group). Cross-region arbitration: if regional pool exhausted, a coordinated auction with adjacent regions can trigger spillover bids with higher unit cost.
Telemetry: record bid_id, endpoint, pool, units_requested, units_awarded, mitigation_action, pre/post wallet balance, and reconciliation status to tracing and metrics.
Security: only platform governance service can debit wallets; endpoints cannot self-issue unlimited bids — need route-level gating and RBAC.
decisions: Prototype will use second-price sealed bids rather than first-price to reduce strategic overbidding (DECIDED 2026-01-22)
Ledger storage will be append-only blobs linked to endpoint ids and sharded by region for scalability (DECIDED 2026-01-28)
Start with 'soft currency' (no real money) to iterate rapidly; we will add billing hooks in a follow-up once policy matures (DECIDED 2026-02-02)
Operator overrides will be limited to platform SRE runs and exposed via Console with audit logging (DECIDED 2026-02-11)
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: finalize SLO->unit conversion spec and examples for 3 canonical routes (chat-low-latency, chat-high-quality, embeddings-bulk)
Week 3-4: wallet service prototype + API; unit tests and local ledger integration
Week 5: auction simulator run against 30-day historical traffic for two regions; produce allocation heatmaps and oscillation analysis
Week 6: deploy to staging, integrate console view, and run a controlled overload test with chaos tooling
Week 7: incorporate safety cap feedback and run cross-region spillover scenario
Week 8: ship experiment behind feature flag to 5% of traffic for low-risk endpoints
Post-launch: collect burn/recovery metrics, iterate on unit conversion, and draft runbook for operator escalation
qa_plan: Unit tests for conversion logic with boundary cases (zero traffic, burst spikes, long sequences)
Integration tests for wallet debit/credit sequences including network partitions (simulate eventual consistency)
Load test the auction coordinator with synthetic bids to validate latency under high contention
Chaos experiment: kill cache pods and validate auction award triggers reserve-kv action and that reconciliation completes within SLA
Security review of wallet API to ensure only governance service can debit accounts
